summary: Overview of shadowing methods (shadow maps, Virtual Shadow Maps, ray-traced, distance field, Lightmass baked) chosen by light Mobility, plus per-light shadow properties (source radius/angle, attenuation radius, contact shadows, bias, cascaded shadow maps, far shadows) and performance tips for dynamic lights.
gotchas: Default shadow mapping does not support Nanite geometry and needs manual shadow distance setup
Static/Stationary lights show 'Preview' shadows until lighting is built
Lumen cannot be combined with baked global illumination
Contact shadows are screen-space and limited to what the camera sees

summary: Explains how skeletal meshes render via GPU Skin Vertex Factory, the compute Skin Cache, or the Deformer Graph, covering sections/chunks, 8/16-bit bone indexes, max bones per section, unlimited bone influences, recompute tangents, and Skin Cache debug visualizations.
gotchas: 16-bit bone index and unlimited bone influences need an editor restart and re-import of existing meshes
Hardware Ray Tracing and hair strands require the Skin Cache path
Recompute Tangents processes chunks independently and can show seams at chunk borders
Deformer Graph plugin is Beta; Skin Cache visualizations are disabled in packaged builds

summary: Covers importing OpenVDB files as static or animated Sparse Volume Textures and rendering them via Heterogeneous Volume actors, Volumetric Fog, or Volumetric Clouds, including material sampling nodes, Blueprint playback with the Animated SVT controller and Sequencer, and streaming tuning.
keys: Set Sparse Volume Texture Parameter Value
gotchas: Experimental feature
VDB import only works in Windows editor builds; runtime supports DX11/DX12 SM5/SM6
Not supported on the Mobile Renderer
Page table limited to 2 GB; max 32k on X/Y and 16k on Z; double formats converted on import

summary: Hub page for the Substrate material framework (replaces fixed shading models and blend modes); links to the Substrate overview, the programmer guide on Substrate GBuffer formats, and Epic developer blog articles on F0/F90, layering, thin film, and fuzz.
gotchas: Substrate is Beta

summary: Shows how to enable the Sun Position Calculator plugin and place the SunSky actor (Directional Light, Sky Light, SkyAtmosphere) for a geographically accurate time of day driven by latitude, longitude, time zone, date, DST and Solar Time.
keys: Extend default luminance range in Auto Exposure settings
gotchas: Scene appears bright white unless 'Extend default luminance range in Auto Exposure settings' is enabled or Directional Light intensity is lowered
Remove existing Directional Light/Sky Light/SkyAtmosphere before adding SunSky
Manual Directional Light rotations are reset when other SunSky settings change
Plugin requires editor restart

summary: In-depth reference for TSR, the default temporal upscaler: screen percentage and convergence (stat tsr), Anti-Aliasing scalability group, history/Nyquist history, translucency and velocity, Has Pixel Animation, flicker analysis, history resurrection, ghosting troubleshooting, DumpGPU workflow and the full r.TSR.* cvar list.
gotchas: Epic/Cinematic AA quality stores history at 200% making the history update ~4x more expensive; use High or lower to save GPU
Translucent materials do not draw velocities by default and ghost; enable Output Depth and Velocity
Opaque materials with panning/pixel animation ghost unless Has Pixel Animation is set
WPO driven by animated material parameters needs the Previous Frame Switch node for correct motion vectors

summary: Hub page for the texture streamer that raises and lowers texture mip resolution at runtime; links to the overview, building streaming data, stat metrics, and configuration pages.

Hub page on texture assets: supported import formats (png, tga, psd, exr, dds, tiff, etc.), power-of-two sizing advice, and links to the Texture Graph Editor, Texture Asset Editor, format settings, streaming and virtual texturing.
gotchas: Non-power-of-two textures are never streamed and get no mipmaps
Some GPUs do not support textures larger than 8192 pixels

summary: Hub page listing integrated third-party rendering tools: NVIDIA Nsight Aftermath for GPU crash analysis and NVIDIA SLI Alternate Frame Rendering.

Programmer guide to the game thread vs rendering thread split: avoiding race conditions, UPrimitiveComponent vs FPrimitiveSceneProxy ownership, enqueuing render commands, fences, FRenderResource init/release, and safe GC of static and dynamic render resources.
gotchas: Rendering thread must never dereference UObject pointers without a mechanism preventing GC
RHI functions can only be called from the rendering thread
Do not do per-frame state updates inside DrawDynamicElements; enqueue from game thread Tick

summary: Guidelines for lightmap UVs for baked (static/stationary) lighting: auto-generation on import, custom unwraps, padding, Lightmap Coordinate Index and resolution, Lightmap Density view mode, World Settings lightmap compression/atlas size, and error coloring for overlapping/wrapping UVs.
keys: Packed Light and Shadow map Texture Size
gotchas: Lightmaps are only needed for baked lighting; fully dynamic projects can skip them
Lightmap resolution below Min Lightmap Resolution causes seams and light leaks
Lightmap UVs must not overlap or leave 0-1 space; padding of ~4 texels needed
Error Coloring requires Lighting Quality Medium or Preview

summary: Hub page for Materials: links to essential concepts, physically based materials, Material Editor guide, properties, inputs, data types, Substrate, instances, functions, layered materials, tutorials, expression/function references and advanced topics like Custom Primitive Data and lit translucency.

How to install RenderDoc and use the built-in RenderDoc plugin to capture single GPU frames from the editor (viewport capture button, auto-attach setting, -AttachRenderDoc flag, F12 in standalone) and the plugin's project settings.
gotchas: Reference all resources and Save all initial states significantly increase capture size
Enable Capture Child Processes when launching the editor from RenderDoc

summary: Describes the UV Editor (from Modeling Mode or right-click a mesh) with 2D/3D viewports and tools for sew, split, layout/repack, transform, align, distribute, channels, seams, AutoUV (PatchBuilder, UVAtlas, XAtlas) and unwrap methods, plus UDIM management.
gotchas: Beta feature
UV Atlas method does not work on Linux
Avoid Level Viewport hotkeys in the 2D viewport
UDIMs must be set for backgrounds to display outside the 0-1 square

summary: Full guide to Virtual Shadow Maps, the default UE5 shadow method for Nanite/Lumen: enabling, SMRT soft shadows, directional clipmaps, local lights, page caching and invalidation (WPO, Shadow Cache Invalidation Behavior), static caching, coarse pages, visualization modes, stats, profiling, platform requirements and limitations.
gotchas: Designed for Nanite; non-Nanite geometry is far more expensive, so enable Nanite even on low-poly meshes
WPO/PDO and skeletal deformation invalidate cached pages every frame
Exceeding the physical page pool causes corrupted/checkerboard shadows
Needs DX12 SM6.6 atomics or Vulkan; Subsurface Profile/transmission not supported

summary: Overview comparing Runtime Virtual Texturing (GPU-generated, good for landscape blending) and Streaming Virtual Texturing (disk-streamed large textures, UDIMs), plus enabling virtual texture lightmaps; links to memory pools, settings, and the RVT quick start.
gotchas: Including non-VT lightmaps constrains atlas size and removes some VT lightmap benefit
Lossy VT lightmap compression lowers quality

summary: Explains distance, view frustum, precomputed visibility and dynamic occlusion culling (hardware occlusion queries, HZB, VR round robin), actor bounds scaling, stat initviews counters, and debugging with r.VisualizeOccludedPrimitives, FreezeRendering and Game View.
gotchas: Hardware occlusion results lag a frame and can cause pop-in with fast camera movement
Occlusion culling is disabled in Wireframe view mode
Enlarged bounds reduce culling and can hurt performance and shadow quality

summary: Describes the Env. Light Mixer window for creating and editing a level's Sky Light, up to two atmosphere Directional Lights, Sky Atmosphere and Volumetric Cloud in one place, with Minimal/Normal/Advanced property detail levels.
